source.title: An Adversarial Example for Direct Logit Attribution: Memory Management in GELU-4L
source.authors: Jett Janiak; C. Rager; James Dao; Yeu-Tong Lau

page_placements.theme: Counterbalancing in ordinary forward passes: later components partly cancel or damp earlier writes and confident predictions, with no ablation
Compensation and downstream erasure also distort non-ablation attribution, and blocking compensation changes rankings

record.tranche_reason: The study reports erasure of an earlier head’s output and its effects on direct logit attribution, but does not test whether ablating an attention layer or head causes later components to restore the original prediction.
record.gate_note: The study measures downstream erasure and tests whether it depends on V-composition. It does not ablate a whole attention layer or head and measure restoration of the original prediction. Its attribution results concern DLA, not ablation-based importance scores.
record.test_reason: The study measures erasure: layer-2 heads in GELU-4L write the negative of L0H2's output. It also shows this makes DLA misleading. It never ablates a layer or head to measure whether downstream components restore the output, so no self-repair version is tested. It does not cite either original source; erasure is a related but different construct.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct as paraphrased: a concrete erasure example in GELU-4L, a caution that DLA can mislead under erasure, and recommendations to vary prompts and use activation patching. The authors also note the work covers a single model and head, so generalization is untested.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures projection ratios and DLA contributions in one 4-layer model, and uses zero ablation on a V-composition path to investigate erasure. It does not measure post-ablation restoration of predictions.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured erasure depends on whether V-composition between L0H2 and layer 2 erasing heads is patched; the study also reports that projection ratio falls again after layer 2.

fits_no_version.finding: Six of eight layer-2 heads in GELU-4L write opposite to L0H2, erasing about 90.7% of its output. Removing L0H2 from their value input removes about 85% of the layer-2 erasure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream attention heads can actively erase an earlier head's residual-stream output via V-composition (memory management).

fits_no_version.finding: DLA of L0H2 and the erasing heads is anti-correlated (r=-0.702, slope -0.613). L0H2's DLA stays high even when its input is replaced with unrelated text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream erasure can make direct logit attribution overstate a writing component's contribution.

record.peer_reviewed: BlackboxNLP Workshop on Analyzing and Interpreting Neural Networks for NLP
record.problems: The study focuses on a single model and a specific attention head. Its authors note that generalization across model components and sizes remains untested. Some results are presented in figures with quantile ranges but without exact values in the text.

untested.parts: No attention-layer ablation followed by measurement of downstream compensation.
No late-MLP analysis of downregulating the maximum-likelihood token.
No single-head ablation measuring compensation; single 4-layer model only.
No compensation distribution or overcorrection measured.
Erasing heads are identified, but not as mechanisms of self-repair after ablation.
No comparison of ablation types for self-repair.
Attribution concern is about DLA under erasure, not ablation scores under self-repair.

record.verdict_notes: Erasure here is a feed-forward cancellation present on the clean run, not compensation triggered by ablation. It is adjacent to self-repair (and possibly to copy-suppression) but does not test any version. The four comparison heads in R8 are unnamed.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test layer ablation followed by compensation from later attention layers.
Does not test late-MLP counterbalancing of the maximum-likelihood token.
Does not test single-head ablation and compensation on the full distribution or across model families and sizes.
Does not measure compensation across prompts or report overcorrection after ablation.
Identifies erasing heads, but does not test the named self-repair mechanisms in this version.
Uses zero ablation on a V-composition path to investigate erasure; it does not compare on-distribution ablations with zero ablation for self-repair.
Shows that erasure can make DLA misleading, but does not test whether ablation-based importance scores misstate component effects because of self-repair.

rows.subject: GELU-4L
rows.operation_detail: Measured projection ratio of residual-stream activations onto the output of L0H2
rows.value: Close to 1 after L0H2 writes at resid_mid_0; stays close to 1 through resid_post_1
rows.note: The study reports that L0H2's output remains present in the residual stream through these states.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for self-repair; persistence of L0H2's output is observed.
source_check.problem: The measurement establishes residual-stream persistence, not a self-repair claim version.

rows.subject: GELU-4L
rows.operation_detail: Measured projection ratio of residual-stream activations onto the output of L0H2
rows.uncertainty: Figure 1 shows median and 25th and 75th quantiles
rows.note: The authors attribute the drop to attention heads removing information written by L0H2.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for self-repair; erasure between resid_post_1 and resid_mid_2 is observed.
source_check.problem: Erasure during a clean forward pass does not establish compensation after ablation.

rows.subject: GELU-4L
rows.operation_detail: Measured projection ratios of layer 1–3 component outputs onto L0H2's output
rows.measure: Projection ratio; aggregate erasure of L0H2 output
rows.value: 6 out of 8 layer 2 attention heads had consistently negative projection ratios; together they were responsible for erasing 90.7% of L0H2's output
rows.note: The paper calls these components erasing heads.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for self-repair; heads 2–7 in layer 2 erase 90.7% of L0H2's output; aggregate projection-ratio quartiles are -1.128, -0.907 and -0.700.
source_check.problem: Identifying erasing heads does not measure their contribution to self-repair.

rows.subject: GELU-4L
rows.operation_detail: Zero-ablated L0H2's output from the V-composition path to layer 2 erasing heads
rows.measure: Projection ratio of residual stream onto L0H2 output
rows.uncertainty: Figure 1 shows median and 25th and 75th quantiles
rows.note: The paper says around 85% of layer 2 erasure depended on V-composition; projection ratio fell again after layer 2.
rows.check: Operation is zero-ablation of only the V-composition path (L0H2 output removed from erasing heads' value input), not ablation of a component. It measures loss of erasure, not compensation.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for self-repair; projection ratio after layer-2 attention is 0.91 patched versus 0.12 clean; approximately 85% of layer-2 erasure depends on V-composition.
source_check.problem: Removing the writer's contribution from erasing heads' value inputs measures dependence of erasure, not restoration after component ablation.

rows.subject: GELU-4L
rows.operation_detail: Prevented V-composition between L0H2 and selected layer 2 heads
rows.measure: Projection ratios between erasing heads and L0H2
rows.value: Median moved close to zero in patched run
rows.uncertainty: Figure 3 shows median and 25th and 75th quantiles
rows.note: The authors state that the erasure behavior disappeared when this V-composition was prevented.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for self-repair; erasing-head projection-ratio medians approach zero when V-composition is prevented.
source_check.problem: Disappearance of erasure under path intervention does not establish a self-repair claim version.

rows.subject: GELU-4L
rows.operation_detail: Compared DLA contributions of L0H2 and layer 2 erasing heads

conditions.value: Top 2 next-token predictions at every sequence position

rows.measure: Correlation and best-fit slope between DLA contributions
rows.value: r = -0.702; slope = -0.613; authors interpret the slope as erasing heads removing about 61% of L0H2's apparent DLA contribution on average
rows.note: This is an attribution result about erasure, not a test of ablation-based importance scores.
rows.check: This is about DLA, not ablation-based importance scores, so it does not bear on V7.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for self-repair; DLA correlation is -0.702 and fitted slope is -0.613, interpreted as approximately 61% cancellation.
source_check.problem: DLA cancellation under erasure does not test self-repair or its consequences for ablation-based importance scores.

rows.subject: GELU-4L
rows.operation_detail: Patched L0H2's input with unrelated text from randomly sampled training-data runs

conditions.value: Four constructed prompts for bottom, State, __, and Church

rows.measure: DLA-measured logit difference between the selected token and the second-most-likely token
rows.baseline: Clean prompt; logit differences listed as 1.07, 1.89, 3.02, and 0.94 for the four prompts
rows.value: Patching the L0H2 input with unrelated text did not affect the DLA-measured logit difference
rows.uncertainty: Figure 5 shows medians and 25th and 75th quantiles
rows.note: The authors interpret the unchanged DLA result as evidence that L0H2 did not directly contribute to these predictions.
rows.check: Baseline logit differences (1.07, 1.89, 3.02, 0.94) are clean-prompt values. The patched values are only in Figure 5 and are described as unaffected.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for self-repair; L0H2's DLA-measured logit difference remains unaffected by unrelated-input patching. Listed clean-prompt logit differences are 1.07, 1.89, 3.02 and 0.94.
source_check.problem: Invariance of a head's DLA under input patching does not measure downstream compensation.

rows.subject: GELU-4L
rows.operation_detail: Patched the inputs to four other attention heads with high DLA logit-difference values

conditions.value: The four constructed prompts from Section 3.5

rows.measure: DLA-measured logit difference between top two predictions
rows.value: Results were severely affected by the patch
rows.uncertainty: Figure 5 shows medians and 25th and 75th quantiles
rows.note: The specific four comparison heads are not named in the text.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for self-repair; the four comparison heads' DLA results are severely affected by input patching.
source_check.problem: The comparator establishes DLA sensitivity to input patching, not a self-repair effect.

relation.reason: It investigates related erasure and attribution mechanisms without measuring self-repair.

tranche.reason: The study measures erasure and misleading DLA in GELU-4L; it neither tests nor uses any listed self-repair version.

source_check.notes: The reported erasure and DLA effects are supported. State corrections concern their interpretation against self-repair versions: all rows link to none, and these measurements cannot determine compensation. The supplied text is revision v4 dated 14 December 2024.
